item.description:

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
200 PM HST Thu Aug 27 2026

For the central North Pacific...between 140W and 180W:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on newly formed
Tropical Storm Karina, located well south of the southern tip of the
Baja California Peninsula, as well as newly formed Tropical Storm
Lowell, located well west-southwest of the southern tip of the Baja
California Peninsula, and on Tropical Storm Lala, located several
hundred miles north of Kure Atoll.

Central Pacific:
An area of low pressure could form well south or southwest of the
Hawaiian Islands over the weekend or early next week. Some gradual
development is possible thereafter while the system moves slowly
west-northwestward, well offshore of the Hawaiian Islands.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...30 percent.

&&

header WTPZ31 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCPEP1.

BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Lala Advisory Number  63
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   CP012026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 PM HST Thu Aug 27 2026
 
...LALA SLOWLY WEAKENING AND SOON TO BECOME POST-TROPICAL...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 500 PM HST...0300 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...37.8N 179.2W
ABOUT 650 MI...1050 KM N OF KURE ATOLL
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...40 MPH...65 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NNW OR 330 DEGREES AT 5 MPH...7 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1002 MB...29.59 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 500 PM HST (0300 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Lala was
located near latitude 37.8 North, longitude 179.2 West.  Lala is
moving toward the north-northwest near 5 mph (7 km/h).  A gradual
turn toward the west-northwest is expected tonight.  On the
forecast track, Lala is expected to cross the International Date
line on Friday.
 
Maximum sustained winds have decreased to near 40 mph (65 km/h) 
with higher gusts.  Continued slow weakening is forecast, and Lala 
is likely to become a post-tropical low tonight. 
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 115 miles (185 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1002 mb (29.59 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 1100 PM HST.
 
$$
Forecaster Pasch

item.title: Tropical Storm Lala Forecast Discussion Number 63
item.description:
Issued at 500 PM HST Thu Aug 27 2026 
000
WTPA42 PHFO 280238
TCDCP2
 
Tropical Storm Lala Discussion Number  63
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   CP012026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 PM HST Thu Aug 27 2026
 
Lala is still maintaining some limited deep convection, with cloud 
tops to near -50C, mainly over the southern portion of the 
circulation.  Thus, the system barely qualifies as a tropical 
cyclone although the organization of the convection is marginal.  
Dvorak classifications are T2.0 and T1.5.  A couple of fairly 
recent scatterometer passes indicated that the maximum winds have 
decreased to around 35 kt.  Given the vertical wind shear, dry air 
entrainment, and the cyclone being over cold water, the convection 
should mostly dissipate within the next 12 hours or so  and it is 
unlikely to return.  Therefore, Lala is expected to become a 
post-tropical cyclone by 12 hours.
 
The initial motion remains about the same, or about 335/4 kt. 
A turn toward the west-northwest or northwest is expected during the 
next day or so as Lala becomes embedded in the flow between a 
low-level ridge to the north and a western Pacific tropical cyclone 
approaching from the south.  This general motion should continue 
until the system dissipates. The new forecast track is similar to 
the previous NHC prediction but a little faster in 36 to 48 hours. 
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
 
INIT  28/0300Z 37.8N 179.2W   35 KT  40 MPH
 12H  28/1200Z 38.2N 179.8W   35 KT  40 MPH...POST-TROPICAL
